claims.text: Ask the parent: something the child does that makes them proud; physical well-being or special health care needs; development or learning; weight, eating behaviors, physical activity or sleep; mood or behavior (attention, hitting others, temper, worries, not having good friends, irritability, mood, activity level).
claims.quote: Tell me something your child does that makes you proud. • What concerns do you have about your child’s physical well-being or special health care needs? • Do you have any concerns about your child’s development or learning? • Do you have any concerns about your child’s weight, eating behaviors, physical activity level, or sleep patterns? • Tell me about any concerns you may have about your child’s mood or behavior (eg, attention, hitting others, temper, worries, not having good friends, irritability, mood, or activity level)?
claims.locator: 9 and 10 year visits, Health Supervision: History / Review of Systems

claims.text: Past medical hx: any specialty or emergency care since the last visit.
claims.quote: received any specialty or emergency care since the last visit?

claims.text: Family hx: any new health condition or death in the family; if yes, who has or had it, age at onset and diagnosis, or age at death.
claims.quote: developed a new health condition or died? If the answer is Yes: Ascertain who in the family has or had the condition, and ask about the age of onset and diagnosis. If they are no longer living, ask about their age at the time of death.

claims.text: Ask the child: what they'd like to talk about; questions about their health, body or how it is changing; something they're really good at; what they do to help others.
claims.quote: What would you like to talk about today? • Do you have any questions about your health? Your body? Or how your body is changing? • Tell me something you’re really good at. • What do you do to help others?

claims.text: ROS — any problems with: frequent headaches or dizziness; eyes or vision; ears or hearing; nose or throat; breathing problems or chest pain; belly pain, vomiting, urine or bowel problems; rashes, moles, birthmarks or sunburns; muscle aches, injury or other problems. Girls: have periods started?
